ἐκεῖ ἔλα βον ἀμφίασιν· ἀλλὰ γυμνοῦ, ἀλλὰ πλουσίου. Ἐὰν μέντοι γε χιτῶνά τις ἔχῃ
ἕνα, καὶ τοῦτον τὸν χιτῶνα, προφάσει τοῦ ἀπαιτεῖν τὸ ἐμὸν, ἐκδύσω, μὴ ἐλεήσας
ἐκεῖνον τὸν γυμνὸν, ἀμφίασιν τοῦ γυμνοῦ ἀφειλόμην. Πολλὰ δὲ τοιαῦτα, ἐν ἡμῖν
γίνεται, ὅτ' ἂν δανείζω μεν, ὅτ' ἂν πρὸς ὀφειλέτας ἐρχώμεθα. Πολλάκις ὀφει λέτης
ἡμῶν εἰς ὑπερβολὴν πένεται, μὴ δυνάμενος ἀποδοῦναι· καὶ ἡμεῖς, τὰ σπλάγχνα
ἡμῶν ἀποκλεί σαντες, ἀνηλεεῖς καὶ ὠμοὶ γινόμεθα, μὴ βλέποντες ὅτι γυναῖκα τρέφει
καὶ τέκνα, καὶ μόλις τρέφεται ἀπὸ τῶν ποριζομένων αὐτῷ ὀλίγων ὀβολῶν. Ἀπαι
τοῦμεν πικρῶς ἔσθ' ὅτε καὶ περισσὰ ἔχοντες παρ' ἑαυτοῖς. Ταῦτα οὖν λέγει ἐγκαλῶν
τῷ Ἰὼβ, ὅτι ἀμ φίασιν γυμνῶν ἀφεῖλεν. Στίχ. ζʹ. Οὐδὲ ὕδωρ διψῶντας ἐπότισας·
ἀλλὰ πεινώντων ἐστέρησας ψωμόν. Εἰς τὸ αὐτό. Οὐκοῦν οὐ μόνον τὸ ἀδικεῖν, ἀλλὰ
καὶ τὸ μὴ εὐεργετεῖν ὑπεύθυνον. Ταῦτα πάντα κατηγορήματά εἰσι, καὶ ἀληθῶς
ψεκτά. Ἀλλ' οὐκ ἀληθῆ περὶ τοῦ Ἰὼβ, οὐδὲ καλῶς ἐλέγετο περὶ αὐτοῦ. Τοῦ αὐτοῦ.
Τοιαῦτα γίνεται ἐν ταῖς πικραῖς 17.84 ἀπαιτήσεσιν. Ἐνίοτε αὐτὸν τὸν ψωμὸν ἔχει τις
ἕνα· κἂν μὴ ἔχῃ ἄρτον ὁλόκληρον, ἀφαιροῦμεν ἀπ' αὐτοῦ λέγοντες· Ἀλλ' ὀφείλεις
Στίχ. θʹ. Χήρας δὲ ἐξαπέστειλας κενάς. Προσέχωμεν ἐὰν χήρα ἡμῶν εἰσέλθῃ εἰς τὴν
οἰκίαν, μήποτε κενὴν αὐτὴν ἐξαποστείλωμεν. Κατὰ δύνα μιν ἕκαστος πρὸς ὃ ἔχει
πληρωσάτω τὸν κόλπον τῆς χήρας. Στίχ. θʹ. Ὀρφανοὺς δὲ ἐκάκωσας. Τοῦ αὐτοῦ.
Οὐδένα μὲν δεῖ κακοῦν, ἐξαιρέτως δὲ χρὴ φείδεσθαι τῶν ὀρφανῶν. Περὶ γὰρ τῶν
ἀβοηθή των ψυχῶν πολεμεῖν ὁ Θεὸς ἐνετείλατο. Μᾶλλον δὲ παρὰ τοὺς ἄλλους
ἀνθρώπους, πτωχοὶ, χῆραι, ὀρφα νοὶ δέονται βοηθείας. Στίχ. ιʹ. Τοιγαροῦν
ἐκύκλωσάν σε παγίδες. Παγίδας λέγει τὰ συμβεβηκότα αὐτῷ, ἐν αἷς ἐμ πέπτωκεν, εἰς
ἃς καὶ παγιδεύεται αὐτοῦ ἡ ψυχὴ ἀπὸ τῶν συμβεβηκότων αὐτῷ. Στίχ. ιαʹ. Τὸ φῶς σοι
σκότος ἀπέβη. Ἐν φωτὶ ἦς, ὅτε τὰ ὑπάρχοντά σοι ἦν, ὅτε τὰ τέκνα σου περιῆν, ὅτε
ὑγίαινέ σου τὸ σῶμα. Νῦν δὲ οἷον εἰς σκότος καταβέβηκας, εἰς τὰς περιστάσεις
ταύτας. Εἰς τὸ αὐτό. Τουτέστιν ἐν ἐρημίᾳ, καὶ αἴ θριος, ἀλήτης, καὶ φυγὰς, καὶ
ἀνέστιος. Στίχ. ιαʹ. Κοιμηθέντα δὲ ὕδωρ σε ἐκάλυψεν. Τὸ, κοιμηθέντα σε ὕδωρ
ἐκάλυψεν, τοιοῦτόν ἐστιν· Ἐκάλυψέ σε ἡ ἀντικειμένη ἐνέργεια. Ἐπεὶ οὐκ
ἐγρηγόρεις, ἐπεὶ οὐχ ὕπνωσας. Οἶδε δὲ ἡ Γραφὴ ὕπνον τινὰ ἁμαρτίας. ∆ιὸ ἐντέταλται
ἡμῖν λέγουσα· Μὴ δῷς ὕπνον σοῖς ὄμμασι, μηδὲ νυσταγμὸν τοῖς βλεφάροις, ἵνα ζήσῃ
ὥσπερ δορκὰς ἐκ βρό χων, καὶ ὥσπερ ὄρνεον ἐκ παγίδος. Στίχ. ιβʹ. Μὴ οὐχὶ ὁ τὰ
ὑψηλὰ ναίων ἐφορᾷ; Ἀλλὰ νομίζεις, ὅτι οὐχ ὁρᾷ τὰ πραττόμενα ὁ ἐν ὑψηλοῖς
κατοικῶν Θεός. Οἷα τοίνυν πάντα ἐφορῶν, τοὺς ὑπὸ τῆς ὑβριστικῆς ἕξεως
ἐπηρμένους τὸ φρό νημα καταφέρει. Στίχ. ιβʹ. Τοὺς δὲ ὕβρει φερομένους ἐταπεί
νωσεν. Εἴ τις φέρεται ὕβρει, καὶ οἱονεὶ κατασύρεται ὑπὸ ὑβριστικῆς ἕξεως καὶ
πράξεως, οὗτος ταπεινοῦται ὑπὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ. Εἰκὸς οὖν, ἐπεὶ καὶ σὺ ὕβρισας χήρας καὶ
ὀρφανοὺς, καὶ ἠνεχύρασας διακενῆς τοὺς ἀδελ φούς σου· διὰ τοῦτο ταῦτα πέπονθας,
καὶ τεταπεί νωσαι. Στίχ. ιγʹ. Καὶ εἶπας, Τί ἔγνω ὁ Ἰσχυρός; Εἰκὸς, ὅτι σὺ ἔλεγες κατὰ
σαυτὸν, Τί ἔγνω ὁ Ἰσχυ ρός; Οἷον, ∆ύναται πάντα ἐγνωκέναι ὁ Θεός; Στίχ. ιγʹ. Ἢ
κατὰ τοῦ γνόφου κρινεῖ; Τοῦ αὐτοῦ. ∆ύναται δὲ κρίνειν ὁ Θεὸς καὶ ἐν χει μῶνι
γενόμενος. Στίχ. ιδʹ. Καὶ γῦρον οὐρανοῦ διαπορεύεται. Ἐκπεριέρχεται ἡ πρόνοια τοῦ
Θεοῦ. 17.85 Στίχ. ιεʹ. Μὴ τρίβον αἰώνιον φυλάξῃς; Μὴ δύνασαι σὺ τὴν τρίβον τὴν
αἰώνιον, καθ' ἧς πορεύεται ἡ πρόνοια τοῦ Θεοῦ, ἐπιτηρῆσαι; Στίχ. ιεʹ. Ἣν ἐπάτησαν
ἄνδρες δίκαιοι. Τοῦ αὐτοῦ. Τὴν τρίβον τὴν αἰώνιον ἐπάτησαν ἄν δρες δίκαιοι. Κατὰ
γὰρ τρίβου αἰωνίας βαίνουσιν. Ἐπεὶ πάντα αὐτοῖς πρόκειται πράττειν, ὥστε τυχεῖν
τοῦ μέλλοντος αἰῶνος. Κἂν δοκῶσιν οὖν ἐπίσης βα δίζειν, ἀλλ' ἡ ψυχὴ αὐτὴ
ἐπιβαίνει τρίβων αἰωνίων. Στίχ. ι ʹ. Οἳ συνελήφθησαν ἄωροι. Πολλάκις δίκαιοι πρὸ
καιροῦ ἐτελεύτησαν. Τε λειωθεὶς γὰρ ἐπ' ὀλίγῳ ὁ δίκαιος, ἐπλήρωσε χρό νους
μακρούς· ἀρετὴ γὰρ ἐν τῷ Κυρίῳ ἡ ψυχὴ αὐτοῦ. Στίχ. ι ʹ. Ποταμὸς ἐπιῤῥέων οἱ
θεμέλιοι αὐτῶν. Τοῦ αὐτοῦ. Τῶν δικαίων οἱ θεμέλιοι οἷόν εἰσιν. Ἀεὶ προκόπτουσιν,
ἀεὶ αὔξουσιν ἐν τοῖς ἀγαθοῖς. Στίχ. ιηʹ. Ὃς δὲ ἐνέπλησε τοὺς οἴκους αὐτῶν ἀγαθῶν.
Τοῦ αὐτοῦ. Τῶν δικαίων ἐνέπλησε τοὺς οἴκους ἀγαθῶν. Ἐγὼ οὐκ ἀκούω τοὺς οἴκους
τούτους· ἀλλὰ τοὺς οἴκους αὐτῶν, τοὺς κατὰ τὸ ἡγεμονικὸν ἐνέπλησεν ἀγαθῶν.
Ποίων ἀγαθῶν; Σωφροσύνης, δι καιοσύνης, ἀνδρείας, φρονήσεως, τῶν ἀπὸ τῶν
pass_a_gloss: ...there they took clothing; but of a naked one, but of a rich one. If however someone has one tunic, and this tunic, on pretext of demanding back what is mine, I strip off, not having pitied that naked one, I have taken away the clothing of the naked. And many such things happen among us, whenever we lend, whenever we go toward debtors. Often our debtor is poor to excess, not being able to give back; and we, having shut our bowels, become pitiless and raw, not seeing that he feeds a wife and children, and is barely fed from the few obols provided to him. We demand back bitterly, sometimes also having excess with ourselves. These then he says, accusing Job, that he took away clothing of the naked. Verse 7. Nor did you give water to drink to the thirsty; but you deprived a morsel of the hungry. Into the same. Therefore not only doing wrong, but also not doing good is liable. These all are accusations, and truly blameworthy. But not true about Job, nor were they well said about him. Of the same. Such things happen in the bitter demands. Sometimes someone has the morsel itself, one; even if he does not have a whole loaf, we take away from him saying: but you owe. Verse 9. And widows you sent out empty. Let us pay attention, if a widow enters our house, lest we send her out empty. According to power each, toward what he has, let him fill the lap of the widow. Verse 9. And orphans you harmed. Of the same. One must harm no one, but exceptionally one must spare the orphans. For about the unhelped souls God commanded to fight. More than the other men, poor, widows, orphans need help. Verse 10. Therefore snares encircled you. He calls snares the things having happened to him, in which he has fallen in, into which also his soul is ensnared from the things having happened to him. Verse 11. The light turned out darkness to you. In light you were, when your possessions were, when your children survived, when your body was healthy. But now as it were into darkness you have gone down, into these circumstances. Into the same. That is in desolation, and in the open air, a wanderer, and an exile, and hearthless. Verse 11. And having slept, water covered you. The: having slept, water covered you, is such: the opposing working covered you. Since you were not awake, since you did not sleep. And the Scripture knows a certain sleep of sin. Therefore it has commanded us saying: do not give sleep to your eyes, nor drowsiness to the eyelids, so that you live like a gazelle out of nooses, and like a bird out of a snare. Verse 12. Does not the one dwelling the high places look upon? But you think that God, the one dwelling in high places, does not see the things done. As one then looking upon all, he brings down those lifted up in mind by the insolent habit. Verse 12. And those carried by insolence he humbled. If someone is carried by insolence, and as it were is dragged down by insolent habit and practice, this one is humbled by God. It is likely then, since you too insulted widows and orphans, and took pledges of your brothers for nothing; through this you have suffered these things, and have been humbled. Verse 13. And you said: what has the Strong One known? It is likely that you were saying by yourself: what has the Strong One known? As: can God have known all things? Verse 13. Or will he judge down through the gloom? Of the same. God can judge even being in a storm. Verse 14. And he goes through the circle of heaven. The providence of God goes around. Verse 15. Will you guard an eternal path? Can you watch over the eternal path, along which the providence of God goes? Verse 15. Which righteous men trod. Of the same. The eternal path righteous men trod. For they walk along an eternal path. Since all things lie before them to do, so as to attain the coming age. Even if then they seem to walk equally, yet the soul itself steps on eternal paths. Verse 16 (digit lost). Who were seized untimely. Often righteous ones died before time. For the righteous having been perfected in a little, fulfilled long times; for virtue in the Lord his soul. Verse 16. A river flowing on, their foundations. Of the same. Of the righteous the foundations are such. Always they progress, always they grow in the good things. Verse 18. And who filled their houses with good things. Of the same. He filled the houses of the righteous with good things. pass_b_english: … took clothing there: [not] from a naked man, but from a rich man. If, however, a man has a single tunic, and I strip that tunic off him on the pretext of claiming what is mine, without pity for the man left naked, then I have taken away the clothing of the naked. Many such things happen among us, whenever we lend money, whenever we go after our debtors. Often our debtor is poor beyond measure and cannot pay us back; and we shut up our hearts and become pitiless and cruel. We do not see that he is feeding a wife and children and can barely feed himself on the few small coins he scrapes together. We demand payment bitterly, and sometimes we do so while we ourselves have more than enough. This, then, is what he says in charging Job, that he took away the clothing of the naked.
“You did not even give water to the thirsty to drink, but you robbed the hungry of a morsel” (Job 22:7).

On the same words: So not only doing wrong but also failing to do good makes a person answerable. All these are charges, and truly blameworthy things. But they were not true of Job, and they were not rightly said about him.

From the same: Such things happen when debts are bitterly demanded. Sometimes a man has a single morsel and nothing more; even though he does not have a whole loaf, we take it from him, saying: But you owe.

“And you sent widows away empty” (Job 22:9). Let us take care that, if a widow comes into our house, we never send her away empty. Let each of us, as far as he is able, fill the widow's lap with what he has. “And you ill-treated orphans” (Job 22:9).

From the same: No one ought to be ill-treated, but orphans above all must be spared. For God commanded us to fight on behalf of helpless souls. More than other people, the poor, widows and orphans need help.
“Therefore snares have surrounded you” (Job 22:10). He calls snares the things that have befallen him, into which he has fallen, and by which his soul too is ensnared, through what has befallen him.

“Your light has turned to darkness” (Job 22:11). You were in the light when you had your possessions, when your children were alive, when your body was healthy. But now you have gone down, as it were, into darkness, into these straits.
On the same words: That is, in a desolate place, under the open sky, a wanderer, an exile, without a hearth.

“And while you slept, water covered you” (Job 22:11). The words “while you slept, water covered you” mean this: the opposing power covered you, since you were not awake, since you did not sleep. Scripture knows of a certain sleep of sin. That is why it gives us this command: “Do not give sleep to your eyes, nor slumber to your eyelids, so that you may live like a gazelle out of the nooses and like a bird out of the snare” (Proverbs 6:4-5).

“Does not he who dwells on high look upon all?” (Job 22:12). But you think that God, who dwells on high, does not see what is done. As one who looks upon all things, then, he brings down those whose minds are puffed up by a habit of insolence. “And those carried along by insolence he has brought low” (Job 22:12). If anyone is carried along by insolence and, as it were, swept away by a habit and practice of insolence, he is brought low by God. It is likely, then, that since you too treated widows and orphans with insolence and took pledges from your brothers for nothing, this is why you have suffered these things and been brought low.

“And you said: What has the Mighty One known?” (Job 22:13). It is likely that you said to yourself: What has the Mighty One known? As if to say: Can God have known everything? “Or will he judge through the thick darkness?” (Job 22:13).
From the same: God is able to judge even when he is in a storm.
“And he goes about the circle of heaven” (Job 22:14). The providence of God goes the whole way round.

“Will you keep watch on the everlasting path?” (Job 22:15). Can you really keep watch on the everlasting path along which the providence of God travels? “Which righteous men have trodden” (Job 22:15).

From the same: Righteous men have trodden the everlasting path. For they walk along an everlasting path, since everything lies before them to do so that they may attain the age to come. So even if they seem to walk just as others do, their soul itself still sets foot on everlasting paths.

“Who were seized before their time” (Job 22:16). The righteous have often died before their time. For the righteous man, made perfect in a short while, fulfilled long years; for his soul is virtue in the Lord. “Their foundations are an overflowing river” (Job 22:16).
From the same: The foundations of the righteous are of that kind. They are always making progress, always growing in good things.
“And who filled their houses with good things” (Job 22:18).

From the same: He filled the houses of the righteous with good things. I do not take this to mean these houses of ours; rather he filled their houses, those of the ruling part of the soul, with good things. What good things? Self-control, justice, courage, prudence, those that come from the …
